answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a refundable stake before it may influence shared decisions, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated duplicate identities. Audits can compare signed task histories and test whether supposedly distinct agents repeatedly share control or produce linked behavior; a knoll of accounts is not proof by itself. The horizon is the attacker’s cost: every extra identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture, while a sonnet of fabricated profiles cannot substitute for clean, costly participation.
